According to Mark Gurman's latest "Power On" newsletter, Apple is working to turn its upcoming non-AR smart glasses into another health and fitness platform—but these features are likely not to debut on the first-generation product slated for release next year.

According to his report, Apple had previously set out to develop the Vision Pro as a health platform. The company at the time appeared to be working on a version of Fitness+ that could run on the headset, allowing users to watch workout videos, track their movements, and close their activity rings within Apple's first spatial computing device.

They had originally planned to incorporate some special motion-tracking and analysis features to set the device apart from an iPad or Apple TV. However, due to the weight of the headset, the company eventually abandoned this plan:

But the company is now re-exploring similar concepts through its upcoming smart glasses—though the approach will need adjustments because the glasses have no display.

Fitness features on the smart glasses

Apple's specific plans for the smart glasses remain unclear for now, but we do know that Apple has indeed been continuing to hire talent for this effort. The newsletter mentions:

Two things immediately come to mind: the Workout Buddy feature launched on the Apple Watch last year, paired with heart rate sensors potentially built into the glasses—similar to the technology first adopted in the AirPods Pro 3. This combination has a good chance of making the glasses a practical companion for running.

The cameras can also come in handy across different workout scenarios, letting the system understand whether your movements are correct, thereby helping you improve your training performance.

What Apple ultimately delivers remains to be seen. As mentioned at the outset, these features are very likely not to appear on the first-generation model—so we may have to wait a few more years to see the full picture of Apple's efforts in this area.
